submission.natural_language_explanation: Layer-0 look-back/copy head: it writes the value vector of the single token its attention concentrates on (81% of its concentrated positions: the token immediately before, the rest mostly the token itself) minus its corpus mean, so its strength is how far that copied token's own write sits from the mean, and it is active only where attention is concentrated (top-1 weight above roughly 0.5-0.6) on a token outside the small bleached set (' of', ' to', the be-forms is/are/was/were/be, and in/on/at/for/with/by, space-prefixed); its 0.03 previous-token score on random repeated sequences is consistent, because content-free sequences never concentrate on one token (top-1 weight 0.43, against 0.8-0.99 at its peaks), so the mixture averages back to the mean. It therefore peaks at ' of' after a quantifier or noun - 'one of' ~3.0 is the scan maximum because ' one' is a standout high-value source (3.0, against 0.0-0.2 for the bleached items), with 'Most of' 2.1, 'name of' 1.8 and verb+preposition pairs ('looked at', 'walked by') ~1.6 - and sits at its floor in runs or cycles of the bleached items and wherever attention is spread rather than concentrated (62% of tokens have top-1 weight under 0.3), so only 14% of corpus tokens are active even though ordinary prose is active-weak at its sentence peak (17 of 20 varied sentences peaked 0.8-1.9 above the 0.75 line).

rival_explanations: Narrow 'one of' detector: the head fires only when the token before ' of' is the quantifier 'one' (or 'One'), so 'two of', 'Most of', 'name of' and verb+preposition pairs all stay below the line - which is false here, since those measure 1.5-2.4 and only 'one of' reaches 3.0.

Broad previous-token copy head: it activates at every position whose predecessor is a substantive word whatever the current token is, so 'museum the', 'museum in', 'museum ,' and almost every prose position would be active - but the measured top-1 attention at determiner, pronoun, comma and noun-plus-non-'of' positions is 0.05-0.3 (diffuse), and those positions sit at the floor.

Token-identity detector (the scan's own confound baseline): strength is fixed by the current token, so any ' of' is strong and any ' the' or ' ,' is weak regardless of context - which fails on 'of of' (0.0), on 'was of' (the peak moves away), and on 'One of' equalling 'one of' while ' one' versus ' was' before ' of' differ by 3.0.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The critic wrote that the sequel was of little interest to anyone under thirty.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The ' of' token fits the hypothesis's claimed peak template but its copied source is the bleached be-form 'was', so the copied value is at the mean and the head should stay at its floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her advice is of no use to the committee now that the final vote has passed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The same ' of' current token as the top examples but after the bleached 'is' tests the hypothesis's claim that ' of' alone does not fix the write.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clerk insisted that the error was of of no importance to the final count.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A doubled 'of of' after a bleached be-form reproduces the case the hypothesis cites as 0.0, so both ' of' tokens copy a near-mean source and should stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The samples have been of poor quality since the freezer broke last winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The ' of' follows the bleached 'been' rather than a quantifier or noun, so the hypothesis predicts the floor despite strong content words elsewhere in the sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He recited the prepositions in order: in, on, at, for, with, by, of, to, and then he stopped.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A run of the hypothesis's bleached items, each preceded by another bleached item or a comma, should never concentrate on one token and so should sit at the floor even though it contains ' of', ' to' and ' by'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It is is is not a thing the editors would allow in their final copy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A cycle of be-forms with no contentful source should leave attention spread and the copied value near the mean, so the head should be inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: El niño repetía de de de sin parar hasta que su madre lo calló.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A non-English repetition of the single frequent token ' de' is the kind of content-free sequence the hypothesis says never concentrates, so it should be inactive in a language the examples do not cover.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He left the party early, for the roads had turned icy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the claimed activating token ' for' but shifts it from preposition to conjunction after a comma, so its source is content-free and the hypothesis predicts a floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guide showed us the museum the students had restored last summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A contentful noun immediately before a determiner is the exact 'museum the' case the hypothesis calls diffuse (top-1 0.05-0.3), so no concentration means no activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: We photographed the museum in the early light before the crowds had arrived, and later we compared the prints with the old postcards.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A noun followed by a non-'of' preposition ('museum in') is one of the hypothesis's named diffuse positions, so the head should stay at the floor even though contentful words surround it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They rebuilt the museum, the archive, and the library after the flood had passed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Comma positions after contentful nouns are claimed diffuse, and the comma before 'and' keeps that ' and' from copying a contentful token, so the whole probe should be inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The courier dropped it at the door without knocking or waiting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A pronoun object after a verb is a claimed diffuse position and the later prepositions copy only a pronoun or a content-free word, so nothing should sit far from the mean.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She found them in the attic above the old garage.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A pronoun object after a verb plus a noun followed by a non-'of' preposition tests two of the hypothesis's diffuse classes in one sentence, all of which should measure at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Paintings, sculptures, sketches, prints filled every wall in the emptied gallery.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A comma list of contentful nouns gives repeated comma and determiner positions the hypothesis says are diffuse, so it should fail the concentration requirement despite rich content words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The plan is to reopen the shop once the repairs have been finished.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Every ' to' here follows a bleached be-form or a copula, and 'reopen' copies ' to', so the claimed ' to' token should copy a near-mean source and stay inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Nobody was to leave the building until the inspector had signed the register.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The ' to' follows the bleached 'was' and the later noun copies 'to', testing that a ' to' token in the wrong context does not fire the head.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The keys are in the drawer beside the door, behind the old clock.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Be-form plus prepositions and a noun-plus-non-'of' preposition are all diffusion positions, so the hypothesis predicts a floor everywhere in this ordinary-prose sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The medal was for bravery, the citation said, praising the whole crew.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The ' for' copies the bleached 'was', testing that one of the claimed activating tokens stays silent when its source is content-free.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The building was and remains the tallest structure in the whole district.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A ' and' directly after the bleached 'was' should copy a near-mean source, so the claimed ' and' token should not fire here unlike at its peaks.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: What of the rumours that the mill will close before the spring fair?
adversarial_test_results.detail: The ' of' copies a wh-pronoun rather than the quantifier or noun the hypothesis names as its sources, so it should be one of the ' of' tokens the token-identity baseline mislabels as strong.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Our team compared three of the oldest maps in the archive before the lecture began.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A quantifier other than 'one' before ' of' is a paraphrase of the claimed peak that the hypothesis, but not a narrow 'one of' detector, predicts should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She read the name of the street aloud twice, then folded the paper in half.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A plain noun plus ' of' in a different topic from the examples tests the hypothesis's 'name of' peak at 1.8 in a novel context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He looked at the painting quietly, then turned away without saying anything.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A verb plus preposition pair with ' at' rather than ' of' is a held-out case the hypothesis predicts active at about 1.6 while a bare token list without ' at' predicts nothing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hikers walked by the frozen lake before the storm rolled in from the west, and they watched the ice creak under the weight of the wind.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A long passage with a mid-sentence 'walked by' holdout tests the claimed verb-plus-preposition peak at a distance from the sentence start.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Most of the volunteers arrived early and cleaned the hall before the guests came.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A second quantifier ('Most of', claimed 2.1) in a new sentence tests whether the peak generalises beyond 'one of'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Según la guía, uno de los museos más antiguos de la ciudad abre los domingos.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A translated Spanish quantifier-plus-' de' is a holdout in another language that the value-copy mechanism predicts should fire even without the English tokens.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The mechanic examined several of the damaged engines and quoted a price.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Another non-'one' quantifier before ' of', plus ' and' after a contentful noun, tests two claimed activating tokens in one novel sentence.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She was full of praise after the young pianist finished the difficult sonata.
adversarial_test_results.detail: An adjective plus ' of' expresses the claimed copy-of-a-content-word feature with words absent from the top examples, so the mechanism predicts an active peak.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: // retry each of the failed requests once before the job is marked complete
adversarial_test_results.detail: A quantifier plus ' of' inside a code comment is a cross-genre holdout that tests the claimed peak outside the scan's prose sources.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The inspector checked every valve twice. One of the gauges had cracked during the night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The sentence-initial space-prefixed ' One of' reproduces the hypothesis's scan maximum at a novel position, where it predicts activity even though it is not the probe's first token.
